title: Coastal Prawn Biryani
community: Swahili coast — seafood biryani for the greatest occasions
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Coastal Prawn Biryani — a magnificent seafood biryani with prawn shell stock-cooked rice, large sautéed prawns, fried onions, saffron, and the full Zanzibar spice array, sealed dum-style. The grandest seafood celebration rice of the Swahili coast.
longDesc: Prawn biryani is the Swahili coast's grandest seafood celebration — the technique of biryani applied to the Indian Ocean's finest prawn. The prawn shell stock gives the rice an extraordinary depth, and the dum sealing creates a fragrance that announces a great occasion.
ingredients: ½ tsp saffron in warm water
// Prawn Stock: shells + 4 cups water + 1 onion + 2 garlic + 1 tsp salt
steps: Marinate prawns in yogurt-spice mixture 30 minutes.
Make prawn stock: simmer shells in water with onion and garlic 20 minutes. Strain.
Parboil rice in prawn stock to 70%.
Sauté marinated prawns in ghee 3—4 minutes. Set aside.
Layer: half rice, half fried onions, sautéed prawns, remaining rice, saffron water, remaining ghee, remaining onions.
Seal with foil. Dum over lowest heat 20 minutes.
Break seal at table. Garnish with coriander.
chefTips: The prawn stock is liquid gold — do not skip.
Prawns are pre-cooked — they only need 3—4 minutes. Do not dum raw prawns.
Break the seal at the table for the fragrance ceremony.
cookingScience: See TZA084 for prawn stock science and TZA121 for dum biryani science.
sustainabilityTips: Using prawn shells for stock — zero waste.
culturalNote: Prawn biryani is Zanzibar's most spectacular celebration rice — when the dum seal is broken at the table and the fragrance of prawn, saffron, and spice escapes into the room, every person present knows something magnificent has been prepared.
